item.title: After Days of Digital Outages, Americans Wonder if the Country Is Breaking
item.description: The digital outages that began on Thursday may not be linked, but they have left Americans with a sense that the nation is off-kilter, with no one ready to fix it.
item.dc:creator: Sabrina Tavernise, Georgia Gee and Madaleine Rubin
item.media:description: Flights were halted for hours on Friday after officials issued a nationwide ground stop.

item.title: A.I. Helps Find Major Security Bug in Java, a Software Platform Vital to the Internet
item.description: The discovery by security company Calif shows A.I.’s ability to find gaping security holes in popular software. The Java flaw pointed to vulnerabilities in systems used by nearly all Fortune 500 companies.
item.dc:creator: Dustin Volz and Dylan Freedman
item.media:credit: Saumya Khandelwal for The New York Times
item.media:description: Calif, a tech start-up, said it had used OpenAI’s recently released GPT-6 Cyber model to uncover a critical software bug in Java.

item.title: Apple Addresses Outages Affecting Apple Pay, iCloud and Apps
item.description: The disruption followed days of unrelated problems in the past week that interrupted air travel and work at offices, schools and government.
item.dc:creator: Amanda Holpuch
item.media:description: Apple said it was addressing problems with its systems after an internal update caused outages to some of its services.

item.title: Nvidia Has No Plans to Bring Back Jensen Huang
item.description: As the former chief executive and his allies lobbied for his return, the company’s chair said the board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as C.E.O.”
item.dc:creator: Tripp Mickle and Kalley Huang
item.media:credit: Mikayla Whitmore for The New York Times
item.media:description: Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned as Nvidia’s chief executive after reports of a relationship with a company customer and an employee.

item.title: Measles Is Officially Back
item.description: Also, public schools are closing as enrollment drops. Here’s the latest at the end of Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Cullen

item.title: White House Withdraws Nomination of Heidi Overton to Be F.D.A. Commissioner
item.description: The Senate health committee was scheduled to vote on her nomination Wednesday morning, but it became increasingly clear that she did not have enough support.
item.dc:creator: Christina Jewett
item.media:description: Heidi Overton during a Senate committee hearing in September.

item.title: Markwayne Mullin Defends Flight to L.S.U.-Texas Game After Ground Stop
item.description: “We still gotta live our lives,” said the homeland security secretary, who is required to use government planes for personal travel. His department said he paid.
item.dc:creator: Madeleine Ngo
item.media:credit: Tierney L. Cross for The New York Times
item.media:description: Markwayne Mullin, the homeland security secretary, spoke to reporters outside the White House on Friday.

item.title: Hegseth Nominates His Former Aide to Lead the Army
item.description: After months of delay, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and the White House have sent Gen. Christopher LaNeve’s nomination for Army chief of staff to the Senate.
item.dc:creator: Greg Jaffe, Adam Entous and Eric Schmitt
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: Gen. Christopher LaNeve, the acting Army chief of staff, testifying before a House committee in May. He previously worked as Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s senior military aide.

item.title: For Democrats, a Leadership Fight Is Marring an Electoral Triumph
item.description: The contest between Senators Chuck Schumer and Chris Van Hollen to be majority leader is sowing party divisions and putting them on public display.
item.dc:creator: Michael Gold and Carl Hulse
item.media:description: Senator Chuck Schumer of New York, the minority leader, at a news conference at the Capitol on Tuesday.

item.title: With House Democratic Majority Still Growing, Recounts Are Starting in Closest Races
item.description: The exact size of the Democratic majority in Congress was undetermined as recounts were sought in two races in North Carolina and one in Minnesota two weeks after the elections.
item.dc:creator: John Yoon
item.media:description: Democrats secured a 257th seat after a race call in North Carolina on Tuesday, but some races remain uncalled.

item.title: Hakeem Jeffries Embraces Medicare Expansion on Eve of Speaker Vote
item.description: The top House Democrat endorsed lowering the eligibility age, covering all children and adding vision, hearing and dental services, proposals seen as precursors to Medicare for All.
item.dc:creator: Annie Karni
item.category: Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (2010)
item.media:description: Representative Hakeem Jeffries, Democrat of New York, is expected to be nominated for speaker. Before the election, he did not endorse a plan to phase in Medicare for All. But with the Democrats’ sweeping gains, he appears to be taking a more ambitious approach.

item.title: Iran Is Emboldened After Trump and GOP’s Election Losses, Officials Say
item.description: Iran’s negotiating position has hardened since the midterms, U.S. and other Western officials say. An American lawmaker warned that Iran felt “strategically empowered.”
item.dc:creator: Julian E. Barnes, Dustin Volz and Farnaz Fassihi
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Arash Khamooshi/Polaris for The New York Times
item.media:description: A banner depicting Steve Witkoff, President Trump, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Vice President JD Vance was set on fire during a demonstration in Tehran this month.

item.title: Will a Spy Scandal, Trade Friction and a Surprise Guest Ruin Xi’s Big Moment?
item.description: The leader wants the APEC summit to showcase China’s strengths, but he faces export worries and an unpredictable Trump, who has floated meeting Kim Jong-un.
item.dc:creator: David Pierson
item.media:description: Xi Jinping, China’s leader, at a meeting in Shenzhen, China, on Tuesday. By hosting the APEC summit in the technology hub, Mr. Xi may be hoping to make the case that China’s growth can benefit the world.

item.title: U.S. Loses Its Measles Elimination Status, a Historic Setback for American Health
item.description: The nation was once regarded as a global leader for reining in the highly contagious virus. Now, large outbreaks that sicken thousands could become routine.
item.dc:creator: Teddy Rosenbluth

item.title: 26 More Measles Cases in New York, but Outbreak Appears to Be Easing
item.description: The state has recorded over 270 cases this year, the most since a major outbreak of the illness in 2018 and 2019. More than two dozen cases were recorded this past week.
item.dc:creator: Joseph Goldstein
item.media:description: With New York experiencing a measles-related health emergency, medical centers are issuing warnings to patients.

item.title: Democrats Assail RFK Jr. After U.S. Loses Measles Elimination Status
item.description: Incoming senators and prospective presidential candidates blamed the health secretary’s history of vaccine skepticism for the rise of measles in the country.
item.dc:creator: Tim Balk
item.media:description: In a statement on Tuesday, Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the health secretary, vowed to “stop measles outbreaks, protect American families, and work to regain U.S. measles elimination status.”

item.title: Do You Need a Measles Booster?
item.description: As cases spread across North America, now is a good time to check your vaccination status.
item.dc:creator: Dani Blum

item.title: Does This Man Have a Right to the Data From His Own Brain?
item.description: J. Galen Buckwalter cheerfully agreed to provide his neural data for a research study. But when he asked for a copy, things got complicated.
item.dc:creator: Vivian Wang and Gabriella Angotti-Jones
item.media:description: J. Galen Buckwalter outside his home in California. He has chips implanted in his brain that record neural data for analysis.

item.title: Matan Kahana Elected Speaker of Israel’s Parliament
item.description: Matan Kahana, a lawmaker from Gadi Eisenkot’s party, will take control of the legislative process as the opposition looks to press Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on multiple fronts.
item.dc:creator: David M. Halbfinger
item.media:description: Matan Kahana, an opposition lawmaker, was elected the speaker of Israel’s Parliament on Tuesday.

item.title: Another Storm Is Bearing Down on California
item.description: This week will bring wind gusts up to 70 miles per hour, buckets of rain and some of the first heavy snow of the season, forecasters said.
item.dc:creator: Amy Graff
item.media:credit: Mike Kai Chen for The New York Times
item.media:description: Huge waves crashed ashore at Half Moon Bay, Calif., on Saturday.

item.title: National Book Award Finalist May Be Ineligible for the Prize
item.description: The writer Abdelrahman ElGendy was blocked from visiting the United States to attend this year’s National Book Awards ceremony. Though his memoir is a finalist for the nonfiction award, it appears not to qualify.
item.dc:creator: Ronda Kaysen and Ash Wu

item.title: Contested Frida Kahlo Painting Is Withdrawn Hours Before Auction
item.description: Christie’s withdrew the work after accusations that several of the artist’s paintings had gone missing from the Casa Azul house-museum in Mexico City.
item.dc:creator: Victoria Burnett
item.media:description: Christie’s removed a Frida Kahlo painting, “Congreso de los pueblos por la Paz (Congress of Peoples for Peace),” from an auction Tuesday. It depicts a dove perched in a fruit tree flanked by nuclear mushroom clouds.
